title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer ordering during regional failover
author: Asha Mehta
description: Background: During a recent multi-region incident we observed an ordering race in the SLO enforcer that could cause simultaneous backoff and circuit-breaker triggers across regional routing lanes, which in turn produced cascading load-shedding and a spike in 5xx errors. This PR fixes the root cause by serializing critical state transitions in the enforcer and ensuring deterministic ordering when regional failover and backoff policies interact. Motivation: Reduce thrashing and unnecessary global failover during partial regional degradation, restore graceful degradation behavior, and eliminate a regression introduced by ENG-9876 (rework enforcer state machine). Changes: 1) Introduce a lightweight per-candidate fencing token to ensure only one transition path wins during concurrent regional-failover/backoff events; 2) Rework ordering logic in enforcer/decision_engine.go to use compare-and-apply at transition boundary (no global locks); 3) Add new unit tests and a deterministic concurrency test harness that reproduces the previously-observed race; 4) Adjust metrics to tag transitions with the chosen winner and emit a new histogram slo_enforcer.transition_latency_ms for monitoring; 5) Add a short-circuit to avoid duplicate load-shedding policy evaluation when a higher-priority regional failover is in-flight. Risk and mitigation: This touches the SLO enforcer (critical path). Changes were kept minimal and exercised under load in staging across three regions. Added canary rollout: initial rollout to a single region pair for 2h, then full rollout. If instability is detected, automatic rollback path in deployment manifests will revert to previous hash. Testing: - Unit tests cover ordering and fencing semantics. - Deterministic concurrency regression test included (replays the incident timeline). - Staging soak across us-west-2/us-east-1 for 6 hours with synthetic traffic showing 4x reduction in transition thrashing and no impact to tail latency. - CI: build, unit, integration, lint. Rollout notes: Squash-merge followed by immediate canary (1% traffic in us-west-2) and monitoring for slo_enforcer.transition_latency_ms and ado/regional_failover_errors. Related: Linked to ENG-1245 and SRE-987; follow-up to revert a previous workaround in pr-112999.
